plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets and parks turn lavender-purple as trees about 10 to 15 meters tall come into flower. Clusters of trumpet-shaped blooms hang over feathery fern-like foliage. When the petals drop, they leave a violet carpet on the pavement below.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking from October to November
plants.location: Pretoria, South Africa, and across eastern Australia, including Sydney and Brisbane
plants.funFact: Jacarandas come from South America, but Pretoria is nicknamed the Jacaranda City because it has tens of thousands of them. The trees bloom there in mid to late October.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: This tall North American wildflower lights up meadows and roadsides in autumn with daisy-like blooms. Each flower has a golden-yellow center ringed by many narrow rays. The blooms are a vital late-season food source for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn, typically August to October
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, including the northeastern United States
plants.funFact: The flower heads close at night and on cloudy days. Migrating monarch butterflies rely on the nectar to fuel their journey south to Mexico.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Cosmos has airy, feathery foliage and delicate, saucer-shaped blooms that sway on tall, slender stems. It is a cheerful, easy-going garden favorite. It keeps flowering until the first hard frost.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through the first frost, often still in flower in October in mild-autumn regions
plants.location: Gardens in temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere; native to Mexico
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek word kosmos, meaning order or harmony, a nod to the balanced symmetry of its petals.
